Current room drain always one-shots the full list with the two-key effect (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2921-3014) and treats split-required as failure (2934-2940). Node split is nonmutating and happens before issueOneVertex (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6696-6715). copySettlementPlanEffect currently accepts only the two-key replacement shape (packages/issuance-store/src/contract.ts:285-297). If GREEN CAS-upgrades every rebase/transform entry before the suffix probe, a fitting batch is stored as 5-key progress and the one-chunk vectors change. If GREEN probes a still-legacy four-key entry with the 5-key effect, the specified legacy/progress mismatch refuses before any split. Restart after a lazy upgrade also needs the probe to switch effect kind.","correction":"Pin the room order: against a four-key unlinked rebase/transform entry, the remaining-suffix probe uses the existing two-key replacement effect. Only after nonmutating split-required(p) may the room CAS-upgrade that same source to replacementProgress (intentCount = rederived list length, 0 chunks, stored digest) and then issue operations[fromIntent, throughIntent) with the 5-key effect. A later suffix against an already-progress entry always uses the 5-key effect. intentCount===1 and any suffix that Node accepts in one vertex must remain the four-key/two-key one-chunk path byte-for-byte."},{"title":"Merge can drop partial chunks the first time the four-key equality short-circuit misses","evidence":"writeMergedSettlementPlan rebuilds four-key entries and copies only prior.replacementSequence (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2864-2909). sameSettlementEntry ignores any future replacementProgress (2835-2839), so an unchanged source set accidentally keeps stored progress via the short-circuit, but any fence-clear or entry-set change rewrites the plan without chunks. f5b0r already clears a displaced fenceSequence and drops sources that now classify terminal (design.md:208-215, 384-387). Test 5 and review item 5 require crash/restart plus close/reopen with no skipped/duplicated intents (plan:99560-99563). A rewrite that turns a partial-progress entry back into a four-key unlinked row would re-issue already committed chunk sequences; dropping the entry would skip the remaining suffix. settlementPlanPermitsAuthenticatedPruning still keys only on the scalar (packages/issuance-store/src/maintenance.ts:110-126), which is correct only if partial progress stays scalar-null and is retained until the final chunk."},{"title":"16 is the correct count ceiling, but the RED split matrix is not causal unless it names the existing byte-budget split","evidence":"APPLICATION_BATCH_MAX_ENTRIES is 16 and APPLICATION_BATCH_LIMITS.maxBytes is 65,536 (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:235-236, 6696-6715). rebaseIntents emits at most that many child ops from one source vertex (6823-6861). Room transform is 1:1 and must preserve action (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:363, 2988-3008), so replacement count cannot exceed the source vertex. That source already passed the same batch contract when it was issued; drainSnapshot even splits ordinary issue at 16 (2702-2714). SETTLEMENT_REPLACEMENT_MAX_INTENTS=16 is therefore the right intentCount bound (plan:99475-99486), but a legal multi-intent rebase of small ops will usually be accepted as one vertex and never hit split-required. Test 4 still requires genuine split-required and ≥2 replacement vertices for both rebase and transform growth (99556-99559). A RED that uses 17 intents will fail the new bound rather than the missing progress behavior (review item 8)."},{"title":"Ambiguous-outcome and clone/copy seams still bind only the scalar, so the first partial chunk is specified to commit and then fail closed","evidence":"Plan readback must observe digest, prefix, chunk sequence, final scalar and revision (99515-99517; test 2 at 99548-99552). Production still treats a replacement as linked iff entry.replacementSequence === candidate.authorSequence (packages/storage-browser/src/internal/browser-issuance-store.ts:967-983; packages/storage-node/src/internal/node-issuance-store.ts:1061). cloneDurableIssueCommit and copySettlementPlanEffect keep only {kind, sourceSequence} (packages/issuance-store/src/contract.ts:269-276, 285-297). applySettlementPlanEffect currently fills the scalar once (415-438). Under the new projection the scalar stays null until throughIntent===intentCount, so the existing readback would latch ISSUANCE_RECOVERY_CORRUPT on the first durable partial chunk. GREEN includes the three backends, but RED will not be causal unless those exact functions are named as the mismatch matrix rather than a new export."}],"p2":[{"title":"Pin the digest preimage as a dense array of detached operations","evidence":"The formula at plan:99490-99497 is hashDomain(\"ts-drp/settlement-replacement-intents/v1\", encodeCanonical(orderedReplacementOperations)) and says logical time/sequence are excluded. encodeCanonical already accepts arrays (packages/canonical/src/index.ts:12, 296-303) and hashDomain takes (domain, ...Uint8Array[]) (561-566). The JS value is still unnamed, so a wrapper record vs a dense operation array would fail-closed on reopen.","disposition":"State that orderedReplacementOperations is the dense Array of detached replacement operation records after expire-filter and transform, in source.intents order, with no logicalTime or authorSequence wrapper, encoded with default canonical limits."},{"title":"Pin Node JSON nested-digest grammar","evidence":"Browser keeps DATABASE_VERSION=2 and the fourth store settlementPlans (packages/storage-browser/src/internal/browser-issuance-store.ts:51-53, 1284). Node keeps entries_json and currently serializes only the four keys, converting only top-level sourceDigest from number[] (packages/storage-node/src/internal/node-issuance-store.ts:376-412). An intentDigest left as number[] will fail copySettlementPlanEntry and surface as ISSUANCE_RECOVERY_CORRUPT.","disposition":"When replacementProgress is present, JSON must include version, intentCount, intentDigest as a 32-byte 0..255 integer array using the sourceDigest convention, and chunks as {replacementSequence, throughIntent}; the Node decoder must convert that nested digest before copySettlementPlan."},{"title":"Pin digest-mismatch error ownership","evidence":"Plan:99510-99517 maps malformed durable values to ISSUANCE_RECOVERY_CORRUPT, invalid caller effect shape to ISSUANCE_COMMIT_INVALID, and structurally valid stale comparison to ISSUANCE_RETRY_REQUIRED. Room resume mismatch is only 'fails closed and does not issue' (99496-99497). Node range-vs-operations.length is an issue-path check (99503-99506) and today would be localIssueFailure rather than an ISSUANCE_* code (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6243-6258, 6691-6715).","disposition":"Room rederive mismatch: throw before issueLocal and do not rewrite the plan. Effect digest/prefix/revision mismatch against a well-formed stored progress row: ISSUANCE_RETRY_REQUIRED. Unknown extra keys / non-closed 5-key effect / fromIntent/throughIntent/intentCount not safe integers: ISSUANCE_COMMIT_INVALID. Node operations.length !== throughIntent-fromIntent: existing malformed-input, before transactIssue."}],"summary":"f5b0t is the right blocking prerequisite: the scalar replacementSequence / two-key planEffect / one-shot room drain cannot represent crash-safe split-required progress, and parent f5b plus the 64-writer/three-close matrix stay blocked unchanged. The additive 5-key progress grammar, 16-count ceiling, fence-first rule, scalar-gated prune, fail-closed old readers, and unchanged browser v2 / Node table shape are the right shape. Before tests-only RED, pin (1) lazy two-key probe then CAS-upgrade only after nonmutating split-required so one-chunk vectors stay byte-identical, (2) merge copies replacementProgress and never blanks partial chunks, (3) RED split fixtures use the existing 65,536-byte batch prefix split rather than intentCount>16, and (4) copy/clone/readback bind chunk sequence while the scalar is still null."}

the result union is closed (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:540-549) and the existing effect-shape rejection uses \\\"malformed-input\\\" (v3-live.ts:6257), leaving RED authors to guess between malformed-input and issuance-rejected.\",\"disposition\":\"Name the exact kind for the count/range mismatch (recommend \\\"issuance-rejected\\\" for a structurally valid effect that fails the plan comparison, keeping \\\"malformed-input\\\" for shape errors) so the RED vectors are deterministic and the store-layer ISSUANCE_* taxonomy stays cleanly separated from the Node-layer kinds.\"}],\"summary\":\"The f5b0t contract is sound on its hard cores: the chunk append is atomic with vertex/lineage/outbox/plan in all three backends with rollback-before-mutation (packages/issuance-store/src/conformance.ts:304-344; browser single strict four-store transaction at packages/storage-browser/src/internal/browser-issuance-store.ts:189 with unchanged DATABASE_VERSION=2 and settlementPlans store at :52-53; Node BEGIN IMMEDIATE/ROLLBACK with in-transaction plan CAS at packages/storage-node/src/internal/node-issuance-store.ts:929-1010); the binding chain (intent digest over ordered operations, fromIntent == durable prefix enforced in-transaction, count equality enforced pre-issuance by Node, chunk sequence filled from the allocated authorSequence, scalar set only at completion) gives crash-safe exactly-once within an epoch including ambiguous-outcome readback; 16 is the correct bound, matching the admitted-batch ceiling (v3-live.ts:235, :6169) and the room's 1:1 intent mapping; legacy four-key entries and two-key effects decode byte-for-byte and old readers fail closed via the exact-key validators (contract.ts:286-319); the commit itself touches only the plan document and the contract authorizes no wire, protobuf, authority, cryptography, threshold, workload, or public-API change, with the 64-writer/three-close f5b obligations explicitly retained (plan blocked section, diff hunk at :18436-18456). One material exactness gap blocks tests-only RED: the contract never states how an open (scalar-null, chunks-present) progress entry survives merge and close, and the natural composition with the accepted parent design's terminal-source removal and displaced-replacement-as-new-source rules admits both silent suffix loss and double-apply — fixable with the three-sentence retention/carve-out rule above. The P2s are actionable polish on serializer symmetry, error-code assignment, bound derivation, constant ownership, and the unnamed Node rejection kind.\"}"}

99430→checkpoint frontier and genuine adoption fixture. The payload-seeded
settlement control set also belongs to f5b. Historical misleading
`[control]` titles remain immutable with a recorded naming caveat. The Node
typecheck exit 2 is inherited and byte-identical to the untouched parent after
root normalization. Future GREEN evidence that runs children against built
Node output must retain the selected built-output path/hash/shape identity in
the evidence pack; f5b0b's final detached checkout rebuilt and passed, so this
is nonblocking prospective evidence guidance.

###### D.110c-0c1f5b0t segmented settlement replacement-progress prerequisite
99440→
**Status: BLOCKING PLAN CHECKPOINT on 2026-09-04.** The first parent f5b RED
stopped before any test or production edit under the accepted design stop rule:
the persisted `SettlementPlanEntry` has only one scalar
`replacementSequence`, `applySettlementPlanEffect` may fill it only once, the
room currently submits all detached replacement intents to one `issueLocal`
call, and Node returns `split-required` before issuing anything. Linking the
first chunk would falsely mark the plan complete; linking only the last would
make earlier issued chunks unauthenticated and unresumable; reusing the scalar
effect is rejected. A room-only retry loop therefore cannot provide exact-once,
99450→crash-safe multi-vertex settlement. This is a demonstrated stored-contract
gap, not permission to weaken the multi-intent acceptance.

Owners: `@ts-drp/issuance-store` contract plus memory/browser/Node backends,
the Node settlement-effect validation seam, and the v3-room settlement drain
owner. Deadline: GREEN and an empty P0/P1 final review union before parent f5b
RED resumes, D.110c-c/d, the same-room 64-writer and at-least-100-transition
gates, the MMORPG golden-path claim, Phase-6 exit, or Phase 7. Because this is
an additive public TypeScript and durable-value contract adjacent to issuance,
one exact Grok 4.6/high, Kimi K3 100-step and Opus xhigh design review is
99460→required before its causal tests-only RED. No production edit precedes RED.

Selected bounded contract:

- Preserve the legacy `SettlementPlanEntry` four-key form and scalar
  `replacementSequence` semantics exactly when the new optional member is
  absent. Add optional `replacementProgress` only for an unlinked
  `rebase` or `transform` entry. Its exact public shapes are:

  - `SettlementReplacementChunk` has readonly numeric
99470→    `replacementSequence` and `throughIntent` members.
  - `SettlementReplacementProgress` has readonly literal `version: 1`, numeric
    `intentCount`, `Uint8Array` `intentDigest`, and readonly
    `SettlementReplacementChunk[]` `chunks` members.

- Export the settlement-owned bound
  `SETTLEMENT_REPLACEMENT_MAX_INTENTS = 16`. Do not replace or import it as
  Node's peer-ingress `APPLICATION_BATCH_MAX_ENTRIES` owner: that existing
  admission constant remains Node-owned at 16, and a behavioral conformance
  assertion pins their equality without creating a future threshold-change
99480→  channel. The bound is exhaustive because an admitted source vertex contains
  at most 16 intents and the room maps each source intent to one replacement
  or drops it; transform remains deterministic 1:1 and cannot expand the
  count. Exceeding 16 is a fail-closed room invariant breach that leaves the
  source and prune gate intact. A progress record has `intentCount` in
  `1..16`, an exact 32-byte digest and zero through `intentCount` chunks.
  Chunk sequence numbers and `throughIntent` values are each strictly
  increasing; every `throughIntent` is in `1..intentCount`. The consumed
  prefix is zero for no chunks and otherwise the final `throughIntent`. The
  legacy scalar remains `null` while the prefix is partial and becomes exactly
99490→  the final chunk's sequence only when the prefix reaches `intentCount`.
  Expire/manual-review entries cannot carry progress.
- The room derives the complete ordered detached replacement-operation list
  before fencing. `orderedReplacementOperations` is exactly a dense ordinary
  array of detached application-operation records in source-intent order after
  the expire filter and deterministic 1:1 transform; it contains no logical
  time, author sequence or wrapper record. Every member must individually
  encode under the existing Node application-batch limits: 65,536 bytes,
  depth 8 and 1,024 items. The whole dense array is encoded under the bounded
  settlement-digest limits: 1,048,640 bytes, depth 9 and 1,024 items. That is
99500→  sufficient for 16 individually valid members plus array framing. Its digest
  is `hashDomain` over the domain below and those exact canonical array bytes.
  This registers that hash name as a device-local durable-plan domain, not a
  wire-bound cryptographic suite or domain change. `intentCount` is the length
  of this post-policy list, not source `intents.length` or `operationCount`.
  Restart/reopen must rederive the exact list and digest; mismatch fails closed
  before `issueLocal` and does not issue, relink, rebuild or downgrade.
- Creation is never lazy inside the issue transaction. For a legacy four-key
  unlinked entry, the room first probes the complete remaining list using the
  existing two-key replacement effect. If Node accepts it, that exact
99510→  one-vertex path and stored representation remain byte-for-byte unchanged. If
  and only if Node returns a nonmutating `split-required(p)`, the room CAS
  upgrades the same source entry through `transactWriteSettlementPlan` to
  `replacementProgress { version: 1, intentCount, intentDigest, chunks: [] }`
  before issuing the first prefix. A later run that finds progress already
  present skips the legacy probe and uses only progress effects. A progress
  effect against an entry without durable progress is refused without
  mutation.
- Preserve the existing two-key legacy replacement `planEffect` for a legacy
  entry. A progress entry requires the additive fields `sourceSequence`,
99520→  `intentDigest`, `fromIntent` and `throughIntent` alongside its replacement
  kind. `fromIntent` must equal the durable consumed prefix; `throughIntent`
  must be greater, no greater than `intentCount`, and the Node issue owner must
  reject before issuance unless `throughIntent - fromIntent` equals the exact
  `input.operations.length`. This validation is internal to the existing issue
  path and does not add a public `V3LocalIssueInput` member. The store
  atomically appends the allocated author sequence plus `throughIntent`, fills
  the scalar only at completion, advances the plan revision, and commits
  issued/outbox/lineage/plan state in the existing transaction.
- The Node owner reads and validates the current plan, digest, prefix and range
99530→  before `buildAndSign`. An effect with extra/missing keys, non-safe indices, a
  non-32-byte digest, `fromIntent >= throughIntent`, or an operation-count
  mismatch returns existing `malformed-input` before signing. A well-formed
  effect whose entry/progress/digest/prefix is absent or different returns
  existing `issuance-rejected`, also before signing and without halting the
  plane. The store retains the authoritative in-transaction recheck. A race
  that fails that recheck after signing returns existing `admission-rejected`,
  halts the handle and requires reopen; it is never retried on the same plane.
  This adds no `V3LocalIssueResult` variant or public Node input member.
- Error ownership is exact. Malformed durable plan values use
99540→  `ISSUANCE_RECOVERY_CORRUPT`. A commit effect with invalid closed shape,
  unsafe indices, `fromIntent >= throughIntent`, `throughIntent > 16`, or a
  range above the selected durable `intentCount` uses
  `ISSUANCE_COMMIT_INVALID`. An absent selected entry, legacy/progress form
  mismatch, wrong digest, or `fromIntent` unequal to the currently durable
  prefix uses `ISSUANCE_RETRY_REQUIRED`; duplicate, skipped and out-of-order
  attempts reduce to that prefix comparison. A plan-write attempt that drops,
  shrinks or changes open progress also uses `ISSUANCE_RETRY_REQUIRED`.
  Nothing in this taxonomy permits retrying a permanent room rederivation
  mismatch.
99550→- Ambiguous transaction outcomes are resolved only by reading back the exact
  digest, prefix, chunk sequence, final scalar and plan revision. If the exact
  chunk link is present, the room drains/publishes the retained pending outbox
  and continues. If a compatible prefix advanced before the pre-sign check,
  it refreshes and continues from that prefix. An unchanged permanent mismatch
  halts. A post-sign/store-recheck or outcome-unknown failure with no exact
  link closes the halted handle and reopens from durable truth; it never loops
  on the same handle.
- The room resumes at the durable consumed prefix. It submits the remaining
  suffix once under the effect form selected above; `split-required(p)` remains
99560→  nonmutating, after which it submits the exact prefix that fits with the
  matching progress effect, publishes it, rereads the plan, and continues.
  Before allocating logical times for any resumed suffix, it authenticates the
  recorded chunk sequences through the existing recovered/accepted vertex set
  and displaced-row outbox classification—no new store lookup API—and sets the
  next logical time strictly above the last operation logical time in the
  latest chunk. A missing or mismatched recorded chunk fails closed. Thus the
  first operation in chunk k+1 is strictly later than the last in chunk k even
  across restart. The settlement fence remains the first issued control
  action, and only the completed scalar permits the existing maintenance gate.
99570→- Plan merge is monotonic for open progress. The room's equality/merge owner
  carries `replacementProgress` byte-for-byte for an unchanged
  `(sourceSequence, sourceDigest, disposition)` triple. The store refuses a
  CAS plan rewrite that drops an open progress entry; removes or changes its
  digest/count; or drops, rewrites, reorders or shrinks its chunk prefix. The
  parent design's terminal-source removal rule is suspended for an entry with
  progress and a null scalar until its final chunk fills the scalar. The
  scalar-null prune gate therefore retains the source row needed for
  rederivation across close.
- Cross-close custody is explicit. A recorded replacement chunk that was
99580→  admitted before close is terminal and is not planned again. A recorded chunk
  that was not admitted and is consequently displaced becomes its own source
  entry under the parent f5b rule; its operations are recovered through that
  new entry, while the original entry's prefix never rewinds and its remaining
  suffix remains its only path. This produces neither duplicate nor lost
  application effects. Only after the original scalar is complete may normal
  terminal-source removal apply. Merge and recovery tests cover both admitted
  and displaced chunk cases.
- Compatibility is additive and fail closed. Old entries, commits and
  one-chunk settlement vectors decode, clone and behave byte-for-byte as
99590→  before. Browser retains the existing fourth object store and database
  version; Node retains its existing settlement-plan table/JSON column. Both
  backends accept exact old and new value grammars and refuse corruption.
  Node's field-explicit JSON writer includes progress exactly, serializing the
  nested 32-byte `intentDigest` as the same 0..255 integer-array grammar used
  for `sourceDigest`; its reader converts both digests before validation.
  Browser structured-clone and all contract clone/copy helpers preserve the
  nested digest and chunks without aliasing. Backend ambiguous-outcome
  classifiers match partial progress by effect digest/range and allocated
  chunk sequence even while the legacy scalar is null. An older binary
99600→  encountering the new member fails closed; it must not silently retry,
  rebuild or downgrade. An old linked entry is complete and can never be
  upgraded to partial progress; only an old unlinked entry may take the
  post-split CAS-upgrade path above.
- No wire envelope, protobuf, checkpoint, anchor, authority, wire-bound
  cryptographic domain/suite, dependency, threshold, workload or public Node
  issue-input change is authorized. The durable/public issuance-store type
  addition and registered device-local digest domain are the entire
  compatibility cost. Do not persist replacement operations. Reject duplicate
  source-plan entries, one plan entry per intent, linking only the first or
99610→  last chunk, scalar reuse, and converting a valid multi-intent replacement to
  manual review or unsupported status.

Tests-only RED acceptance, with controls written so failure is behavioral and
not a missing import/export:

1. Preserve exact legacy entry/effect codec and one-chunk vectors, then prove
   all new shape, bound, ordering, digest, completion-projection and
   corruption refusals. RED uses untyped/`unknown` fixtures through existing
   validators and observable 16/17 bound controls, not imports or type
99620→   annotations for symbols that GREEN has not exported. No 17-intent fixture
   is used as a valid settlement source or progress split.
2. In memory, real Chromium and Node conformance, issue a two-or-more-chunk
   replacement: the first transaction is durable partial progress and the
   final transaction alone fills the scalar. Prove revision CAS, atomic
   outbox/lineage/plan updates, rollback on injected failure, exact ambiguous
   outcome readback, the exact Node-result/store-error matrix above, pre-sign
   versus post-sign handle state, and pre-mutation refusal of every mismatch.
3. Prove legacy migration and downgrade refusal, unchanged browser store names
   and database version, unchanged Node table shape, exact old-value decoding,
99630→   and exact new-progress JSON/structured-clone write/read round trips.
4. Through the real room and Node issue path, make a legal deterministic 1:1
   transform's byte growth cross the existing 65,536-byte batch budget and
   provoke genuine `split-required`, then produce at least two real replacement
   vertices and apply every detached operation exactly once. A multi-intent
   rebase that fits remains the unchanged legacy one-chunk control; no test
   uses a forbidden 17th intent to manufacture the split.
5. Crash/restart before and after the first partial chunk and before and after
   the final chunk, in the same epoch and after close/reopen with both an
   admitted chunk and a displaced chunk. Prove no skipped, duplicated or
99640→   substituted intent, preserved fence-first order, strictly increasing
   cross-chunk logical time, digest mismatch refusal, monotonic merge/readback,
   open-progress source retention and correct displaced-chunk re-sourcing.

The signed initial plan checkpoint is
`cf4b6d820031a546a8013b500be7bfac100a8a3f`. Its single Grok/Kimi/Opus design
round is preserved under `.logs/d110c-0c1f5b0t-plan-review-cf4b6d82/`.
Grok exited normally with a terminal `CHANGES_REQUIRED` JSON object after
progress prose (the strict wrapper therefore records `NO_VERDICT`, not a
cancellation); direct standard Kimi and Opus xhigh also returned
99650→`CHANGES_REQUIRED`. The blocking union was plan-merge loss of open progress,
post-sign stale-prefix refusal halting the plane, unspecified progress
origination, wrong batch-constant ownership, unnamed Node outcomes,
cross-close source/chunk custody and cross-chunk logical time. This corrected
contract adopts those findings in one batch. Every P2 is also discharged here:
the dense digest preimage and bounded limits, post-policy count, registered
local domain, transform byte-growth wording, unknown-fixture RED technique,
nested Node JSON grammar, exact error codes, 16-bound derivation, independent
constant ownership/equality control and existing Node result kinds are now
explicit. One material confirmation of this corrected executable contract is
99660→required; no recursive review of its later bookkeeping prose is permitted.

GREEN is limited to issuance-store types/contract/conformance, the three
backends, bounded test fixtures, the internal Node effect/range validation and
the room settlement-drain loop. Focused tests, affected builds/typechecks,

three-close restart/cold-reopen and explicit 64-active-writer composition; this

**Status: BLOCKED on f5b0t GREEN and its empty P0/P1 review union.** The first

three-proposal reconciliation and the

## ACL transition law

- Retained member (present in both ACLs, any role): frontier copied with its
  scanned `terminalThrough` and unchanged `admissionEpoch`. Losing or gaining a
  role changes nothing in the vector.
- Removed member: dropped. Its unadmitted rows are dead to the protocol; its
  device keeps them; their content is resubmittable after re-admission.
- Added member (fresh or returning, indistinguishable and irrelevant):
300→  `[author, successorEpoch, null]`. Its first accountable vertex is a fence or
  slot 0. Local lineage continues on a returning device and starts at 0 on a
  fresh device; neither needs a store operation, and neither can collide with
  the old incarnation because every old-incarnation vertex is bound to an
  epoch below `admissionEpoch` and to a dead anchor, which ingress already
  rejects (`v3-live.ts:3800-3829`).
- `LatchedAclMember` stays `{author, finalityKey, groups}`
  (`packages/protocol-v3/src/latched-acl.ts:8`); snapshot versions 1 and 2 are
  untouched. Under the settlement profile the ACL is a version-3 snapshot that
  changes only constants (member cap 256, canonical ceiling 65,536 bytes,
310→  decode limits `{maxBytes: 65_536, maxDepth: 4, maxItems: 8_192}`), accepted
  only when `settlementProfileFor(profileId) !== "none"`; the author-list cap
  at `packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:774` rises to 256 under the same
  predicate (D.110c-0c1k W1). Staging enforces exactly the open path's decode
  limits (D.110c-0c1k W0). The incarnation is a checkpoint fact. Authority membership
  (profile/signer-set carriers) and application membership (latched ACL) remain
  separate; a player join is an ACL grant and never an authority change.

320→- Under a verified settlement checkpoint any same-author row at or below
  `terminalThrough` is terminal regardless of digest; the checkpoint
  authenticates a decision boundary, not membership of arbitrary row bytes.
  Same-slot equivocation remains evidence and cannot advance a boundary.
- Rows above the boundary from an older epoch of the current incarnation
  (`admissionEpoch <= epoch < current`) are displaced sources for the plan;
  they are never silently terminal. Old-incarnation rows
  (`epoch < admissionEpoch`) are terminal at re-admission and covered by the
  first fence.
- f5b0d adds the storage-neutral `pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix` contract
330→  from the superseded design unchanged in shape (compare-and-delete across any
  number of old epochs, monotone pruned watermark, expected lineage-next and
  prior watermark, partial deletion fails closed), plus the plan gate above,
  plus its production invocation on every peer after durable checkpoint
  staging, verified adoption, rollback-generation retention, availability and
  expected-head checks, plus the recovery-scan cap correction
  (`v3-live.ts:4349-4355`: `(rollback + 1) × maxEpochVertices` or scan from the
  settled watermark).
- Active control state is one checkpoint of at most 256 triples plus the
  existing rollback generations and history peaks; nothing grows with epoch
340→  count, rebase count or distinct-key churn. Control vertices in the current
  epoch are bounded by `maxEpochVertices`/`maxEpochBytes`; the exposure is one
  fence per author per epoch.

  signer set, quorum and suite to `creator-trusted-v1`; `profileDigest` in the
  genesis anchor binds the choice; old binaries reject it; existing v1 rooms

	/* existing methods */
	readSettlementPlan(scope: DurableIssueScope): Promise<SettlementPlan | null>;
	transactWriteSettlementPlan(input: { scope: DurableIssueScope; expectedRevision: number | null; plan: SettlementPlan }): Promise<SettlementPlan>;

`transactIssue` applies `planEffect` inside the same strict transaction that
writes lineage, issued record and outbox (browser: one IndexedDB transaction
over the exact store set, `packages/storage-browser/src/internal/browser-issuance-store.ts:176-181`;
node: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE … COMMIT`,
`packages/storage-node/src/internal/node-issuance-store.ts:756-800`). For
`fence` it sets `fenceSequence := commit.authorSequence` and fails if already
set; for `replacement` it sets the entry's `replacementSequence` and fails if
the entry is absent, already linked or `manual-review`. The exact-key commit
validator (`packages/issuance-store/src/contract.ts:281`) widens to accept the
optional key. The plan lives in a fourth object store `settlementPlans` keyed
by `[objectId, author]`: browser schema version bump with the exact store-name
check updated (`browser-issuance-store.ts:115-119`, `:1036-1038`); node table
migration in the style of `node-issuance-store.ts:248-255`; in-memory model
and conformance vectors. `pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix` refuses any row
referenced by an unlinked plan entry. No `transactAdvanceLineage` exists: a
lineage jump manufactures consumed-but-absent ordinals that `readIssued`
latches as corruption (`browser-issuance-store.ts:443-447`,
`node-issuance-store.ts:486-490`).

## ACL transition law

- Retained member (present in both ACLs, any role): frontier copied with its
  scanned `terminalThrough` and unchanged `admissionEpoch`. Losing or gaining a
  role changes nothing in the vector.
- Removed member: dropped. Its unadmitted rows are dead to the protocol; its
  device keeps them; their content is resubmittable after re-admission.
- Added member (fresh or returning, indistinguishable and irrelevant):
  `[author, successorEpoch, null]`. Its first accountable vertex is a fence or
  slot 0. Local lineage continues on a returning device and starts at 0 on a
  fresh device; neither needs a store operation, and neither can collide with
  the old incarnation because every old-incarnation vertex is bound to an
  epoch below `admissionEpoch` and to a dead anchor, which ingress already
  rejects (`v3-live.ts:3800-3829`).
- `LatchedAclMember` stays `{author, finalityKey, groups}`
  (`packages/protocol-v3/src/latched-acl.ts:8`); snapshot versions 1 and 2 are
  untouched. Under the settlement profile the ACL is a version-3 snapshot that
  changes only constants (member cap 256, canonical ceiling 65,536 bytes,
  decode limits `{maxBytes: 65_536, maxDepth: 4, maxItems: 8_192}`), accepted
  only when `settlementProfileFor(profileId) !== "none"`; the author-list cap
  at `packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:774` rises to 256 under the same
  predicate (D.110c-0c1k W1). Staging enforces exactly the open path's decode
  limits (D.110c-0c1k W0). The incarnation is a checkpoint fact. Authority membership
  (profile/signer-set carriers) and application membership (latched ACL) remain
  separate; a player join is an ACL grant and never an authority change.

## Recovery, terminal rule and pruning

- Under a verified settlement checkpoint any same-author row at or below
  `terminalThrough` is terminal regardless of digest; the checkpoint
  authenticates a decision boundary, not membership of arbitrary row bytes.
  Same-slot equivocation remains evidence and cannot advance a boundary.
- Rows above the boundary from an older epoch of the current incarnation
  (`admissionEpoch <= epoch < current`) are displaced sources for the plan;
  they are never silently terminal. Old-incarnation rows
  (`epoch < admissionEpoch`) are terminal at re-admission and covered by the
  first fence.
- f5b0d adds the storage-neutral `pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix` contract
  from the superseded design unchanged in shape (compare-and-delete across any
  number of old epochs, monotone pruned watermark, expected lineage-next and
  prior watermark, partial deletion fails closed), plus the plan gate above,
  plus its production invocation on every peer after durable checkpoint
  staging, verified adoption, rollback-generation retention, availability and
  expected-head checks, plus the recovery-scan cap correction
  (`v3-live.ts:4349-4355`: `(rollback + 1) × maxEpochVertices` or scan from the
  settled watermark).
- Active control state is one checkpoint of at most 256 triples plus the
  existing rollback generations and history peaks; nothing grows with epoch
  count, rebase count or distinct-key churn. Control vertices in the current
  epoch are bounded by `maxEpochVertices`/`maxEpochBytes`; the exposure is one
  fence per author per epoch.

## Compatibility, profile and lineage independence

- The creator selects `creator-trusted-settlement-v1` in the canonical profile
  bytes before genesis, exactly as the superseded design specified: identical
  signer set, quorum and suite to `creator-trusted-v1`; `profileDigest` in the
  genesis anchor binds the choice; old binaries reject it; existing v1 rooms
  cannot late-opt-in; no runtime negotiation or downgrade.
- Profile union is implemented as a single exported protocol-v3 predicate
  `settlementProfileFor(profileId): "none" | "v1"`, consulted by the codec,
  `packages/protocol-v2/src/registry.ts:460`, the control-plane normalization
  (`packages/control-plane/src/creator-trust-checkpoint-advance.ts:198-207`),
  the closure validators
  (`packages/node/src/internal/creator-transition-advance.ts:326-328`,
  `:397-398`), the Node close path (`packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:209`),
  reopen (`v3-live.ts:1431`) and the room (`examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:488`,
  `:3985`). No site compares the profile string directly.
  `creator-trusted-settlement-v1` is the last profile ID that fuses an
  authority model with a settlement policy; a later decomposition into
  (authority profile, lineage policy, settlement policy) carried in
  `parameters` changes only this predicate.
- Under the profile: exactly one settlement checkpoint per close; zero
  retirement/aggregate records; every member issues one fence at every open/adopt (one control vertex per
  author per epoch); a null-boundary member cannot advance without a fence or
  slot 0.
- The settlement layer composes with any authority-lineage profile as part of
  the current signed state (`lineage-profiles-impact.md` §2.E). Rotated closing
  authority is `D.110c-0c1j`; author sets beyond the 256-member vector are
  `D.110c-0c1k`; neither is absorbed here.
- Across lineage profiles the plan, fence and incarnation handling are
  mandatory safety (a reconnect after a crash mid-match in an ephemeral-chain
  room is exactly the lost-work trace); pruning cadence, the ≥100-transition
  census and archive cadence are per-profile policy
  (`lineage-profiles-impact.md` §4).

## Crash, attack and failure matrix

| Boundary or attack | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| crash before plan durable | restart re-drains; nothing issued twice |
| plan durable, crash before fence | restart issues the fence once |
| fence durable, unpublished | restart republishes; plan proceeds |
| fence admitted, crash before replacements, close intervenes | boundary = fence slot; sources terminal; restart issues every unlinked entry once in the new epoch |
| replacement issued, crash before the rest | linked entry never re-issued; unlinked entries issued once |
| replacements delayed past close while fence admitted | boundary = fence slot; replacements re-planned as new sources; no double apply |
| fence delayed past close | boundary unchanged; fence and everything after it re-planned; larger `m` next epoch |
| transaction outcome unknown mid-plan | admission halts; reopen enumerates durable truth; no half-link exists |
| rollback after adoption | boundaries regress with the closure; linked entries never re-dispositioned |
| manual-review entry | no fence, no replacements; only that author stalls |
| honest delivery gap (10 delayed, 11 after it) | 11 never admitted without 10; both displaced; plan; fence; advance |
| author absent across two or more closes | rows classified by own signature/scope/digest for any old epoch; no hard failure |
| fence `m > f`, or `m <= s` | ignored; no abort |
| Byzantine fence far ahead | only that author's space burns; recoverable by re-admission on a fresh device |
| Byzantine omission of own predecessor | only that author's boundary stalls |
| same-slot duplicate | author frozen at prior boundary; close proceeds |
| same-key removal and re-entry, same device | new `admissionEpoch`; old rows terminal; first fence at `lineage.next` establishes the base; sequence continues |
| same-key re-entry, fresh device | lineage 0; fence or slot 0 accepted; no collision with the old incarnation |
| stale old-incarnation vertex delivered | rejected at ingress by anchor; ignored by the scan; no equivocation proof for a cross-anchor pair |
| frontier `admissionEpoch` off-rule, boundary regression, vector ≠ successor ACL | rejected by the advance predicate |
| cold open with floor trust only and unknown `priorCheckpointDigest` | succeeds; the opener never requests predecessor bytes |
| codec given only the successor material's key | verifies; no input exists for a current-epoch key |
| control vertex in close graph | in charges/frontier/close-set/history; excluded from the application fold |
| row substitution at or below `terminalThrough` | terminal; never applied |
| legacy v1 room receives fence/profile | unsupported/mixed-profile rejection; v1 unchanged |
| creator's own displaced row | same plan/fence path; no legacy retirement record |
| null-boundary member with no fence and no slot 0 | boundary stays null; close succeeds |
| prune with an unlinked plan entry | refused |
| cross-object migration import | manual-review debt; unchanged |

## Retained findings absorbed

From `solution.md` §4 and the adjudication, each with its owning slice:

- inverted `admittedThrough`/`settledThrough` rules: resolved by one boundary (f5b0a, f5b);
- `readRebaseOutbox` skips published rows (`v3-live.ts:6446`; the D.110c-0c1d record's state-selection-predicate
  freeze is deliberately reopened for the settlement profile only): f5b0b;

  `:5436-5438`): f5b0b;
- no owner for the returning author's lineage: resolved as no jump (f5b0s);
- closure validators reject the new profile: f5b0a;
- prior-less writer check aborts close (`creator-close.ts:517-524`): f5b;
- `completeRebaseSource` is a second completion owner: f5b0b/f5b0c;
- `closeVertices/closeAuthors/closeCharges` do not exist; the complete maps are
  `applicationVertices/...` (`v3-live.ts:7432-7434`): rename in f5b0b;
- nothing prunes in production; recovery-scan cap fails with age: f5b0d;
- non-creator hot follow, journal/snapshot/seal scope retirement, ≥100-transition
  gate, archive-root producer: D.110c-c, D.110c-d, Phase 7, unchanged;
